name: Mount Rushmore
hook: Four presidents, one dynamite-happy sculptor and a Hitchcock chase scene in the Black Hills.

facts.label: Gutzon Borglum
facts.statement: Sculptor Gutzon Borglum designed and oversaw the carving, after deciding the Needles' granite spires were too thin; he had already carved a Lincoln head for the Capitol Rotunda.

facts.label: Washington, Jefferson, Roosevelt and Lincoln
facts.statement: Washington, Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt and Lincoln are carved on the mountain; Roosevelt sits between Jefferson and Lincoln and is the only 20th-century president shown.

facts.label: the Black Hills
facts.statement: It is in the Black Hills of South Dakota near Rapid City, on a peak named for New York attorney Charles Rushmore; the hills were taken from the Sioux after gold was found.
Carving ended in 1941 during World War II, but the memorial was not formally dedicated until 1991 by George H. W. Bush.

facts.label: granite and dynamite
facts.statement: The heads are carved into granite that erodes about an inch every 10,000 years; over 90% of the sculpting was done with dynamite.

facts.label: North by Northwest
facts.statement: Alfred Hitchcock's 1959 thriller North by Northwest stages its climax on the monument, with Cary Grant and Eva Marie Saint clambering over the presidents.

facts.label: the Rushmore State
facts.statement: South Dakota is nicknamed "The Mount Rushmore State," and in 1992 replaced "The Sunshine State" with that motto on its flag.
